## CloudflareApi

Cloudflare’s operationIds are machine artifacts (`zones-get` vs
`zones-0-get` — the `-0-` is a generator’s dedup counter), so rather
than cleaning them up we name every op mechanically from its verb and
path: the group is the path’s non-parameter segments, nested
(`zones.dns_records`), and the method is the HTTP verb — except that
when a group has both a collection GET and a single-item GET they become
`list` and `get`. Two fixups keep the whole surface collision-free:
sibling paths differing only by an interior parameter gain a
`_by_<param>` suffix, and an action segment that would shadow an op
folds into its parent as `<segment>_<verb>`. So `GET /zones` is
`zones.list`, `GET /zones/{zone_id}` is `zones.get`, and
`GET /user/tokens/verify` is `user.tokens.verify.get` — a user who knows
the URL knows the call.

The naming is only trustworthy if it can never silently collide —
`OpGroup` exposes ops with `setattr`, so a duplicate name would shadow
its sibling (exactly the bug this design replaces). This walk asserts
the built tree is clean: within every group, op names are unique
(duplicates allowed only for the same endpoint spelled two ways in the
spec) and no op shares a name with a subgroup.

``` python
def _surface_ok(g):
    nms = [o.name for o in g.ops]
    for n,c in Counter(nms).items():
        if c>1: assert len({tuple(snake(s) for s in o.op_spec.path.strip('/').split('/')) for o in g.ops if o.name==n})==1, f'dup op {g.name}.{n}'
    assert not set(nms)&set(g.subgroups), f'op/subgroup shadow in {g.name}: {set(nms)&set(g.subgroups)}'
    for sg in g.subgroups.values(): _surface_ok(sg)

for grp in cli.groups.values(): _surface_ok(grp)
len(cli.groups), len(cli.groups['zones'].subgroups)
```

    (15, 60)

Listing and fetching zones are now distinct calls: `zones.list` filters
the collection, `zones.get` takes a `zone_id`.

``` python
ucf.zones.list
```

List Zones

Parameters: - name (str, optional) - status (str, optional) - account_id
(str, optional) - account_name (str, optional) - order (str, optional) -
direction (str, optional) - page (float, default: 1) - per_page (float,
default: 20) - match (str, default: ‘all’)

With two domains, the policy must carry two distinct zone resources —
under the old colliding surface the `name` filter was silently dropped,
every domain resolved to the same zone, and the dict collapsed them to
one:

``` python
tok = await ucf.create_token(['answer.ai', 'aaa.as'], ['Zone Read'], 'fastcflare-test-token')
assert len(tok.result.policies[0].resources)==2
tok.success, tok.result.name
```

    (True, 'fastcflare-test-token')

Clean up the token we just created:

``` python
res = await ucf.user.tokens.delete(tok.result.id)
assert res.success
```
